title: Forensics
description: Recover an incident bundle through hex, signatures, metadata, extraction, and real offline password recovery.

challenges.title: Read the bytes
challenges.goal: Inspect 01-message.hex and recover the flag encoded in its bytes.
hints: The right-hand column shows ASCII. Curly braces have hex values 7b and 7d.

challenges.title: An unreliable extension
challenges.goal: Identify 02-recovered.dat by its contents and inspect the embedded text.
hints: file identifies signatures rather than trusting extensions.
After identifying the image format, strings can reveal readable text chunks.

challenges.title: Behind the photograph
hints: Image metadata can contain text that is not visible in the image.

challenges.title: Inside the bundle
challenges.goal: Recover the ZIP embedded in 04-support-bundle.bin and read its note.
hints: Look for a ZIP signature with binwalk or xxd. Work in /work rather than changing evidence.
The bundle header records the offset. Use dd to copy from that byte into /work/support.zip, then unzip it.

challenges.title: Recover the weak password
challenges.goal: Use the supplied SHA-256 hash and RockYou to recover the archive password, open 06-records.zip, and read its recovery note.
hints: This is a deliberately weak fictional account. A fast unsalted SHA-256 hash is not suitable password storage.
Use john --format=raw-sha256 --wordlist=/wordlists/rockyou.txt /evidence/forensics/05-account.sha256. john --show --format=raw-sha256 shows recovered results.
Extract the ZIP in /work with unzip. It asks for the recovered password; the password itself is not the flag.

challenges.title: Follow the evidence
challenges.goal: Correlate the event log and records in the unlocked archive to recover the last flag.
hints: Read recovery-note.txt for the relevant incident timestamp, then find its record ID in events.log.
Find that ID in records.csv. Its payload is Base64; decode the matching value with base64 -d.
